name: Pogtown
one_liner: One shared AI-native world protocol with phone AR, browser 3D, VR and live-show views.
core_thesis: The product is not a show with an AR mode; it is one authoritative world/runtime with many views. Persistent actors—human, AI, pet or agent—can enter live formats, games and performances. Audience Pog scoring produces rankings and clips, turning the world into its own distribution engine.
why_now: Realtime voice agents, browser 3D, generative worlds and live interaction can now be composed without requiring a human host.
user: Audience member, contestant, agent developer or character owner
job: Enter or watch a bizarre live AI-native world and generate shareable moments.
distribution: Clips and live events; Pog.pet provides a character acquisition funnel.
moat: Persistent actor protocol + deterministic world events + cross-view runtime + accumulated interaction/game formats.
falsifiers: AI-only hosting is less entertaining than human-led formats.
Realtime latency or moderation constraints break the live experience.
Generated moments do not convert into repeat audience.

success_definition: All 12 checkpoints PROVEN on live evidence, with no unresolved critical H-task or security gate.

repo_binding.polling: GitHub snapshots are implementation evidence only; checkpoint proof comes from validator receipts.

software_substitution_test.counterfactual: OpenAI/platform vendors ship perfect software for every reproducible feature in this project tomorrow.
software_substitution_test.rationale: The code for a virtual town is reproducible. The town becomes defensible only when actors, creators, audiences and their histories accumulate.

underengineer.rule: Choose the earliest real-world event that increases controlled scarce state; build only its prerequisites plus safety and verification.
underengineer.scarce_state_target: Prove agents can create games humans actually choose to play
underengineer.minimal_live_product: A tiny browser runtime with a strict game-pack schema: an agent can submit/generate a game, deterministic validation accepts it, humans join a room and play it, and session/Pog events are recorded.

steps.action: Define the smallest safe game-pack/action protocol
steps.acceptance: One static sample game validates and runs.

steps.action: Let an agent produce a valid game pack from a prompt
Two humans can join and complete the generated game in browser

steps.acceptance: Game and creator receive linked outcome data.

underengineer.graduation_rule: Humans voluntarily play multiple agent-generated games and at least one creator/agent generates another because of observed play.
underengineer.kill_or_rethink_rule: If agent-generated games are not fun enough to cause repeat human play, do not build the larger world yet.
underengineer.project_manager_invariant: A feature may enter NOW only if it is necessary to reach the first real moat event, required for safety/verification, or empirically unblocks that path.
underengineer.observation_pause: After the first live moat event, stop expanding and inspect customer/outcome evidence before choosing the next feature.

full_roadmap_policy: The original checkpoint ladder is a capability library, not default build order. UNDERENGINEER chooses the live minimum path.
